text:
sqlpipe copies Postgres tables to Amazon S3 as Parquet files. You give sqlpipe a table name and a destination bucket. The tool reads the rows, writes them to Parquet, and puts the files in S3. sqlpipe does a full copy or an incremental sync. For an incremental sync, sqlpipe copies only the rows that changed after the last run.

sqlpipe runs from the command line. You can start it by hand, or you can add it to a scheduler. The tool keeps the Parquet schema in step with your table schema. It also splits large tables into more than one file, and it makes the files a good size for query engines such as Athena, Trino, and Spark. Each run writes a log, so you can see the number of rows and the time of the copy.
